subject: Clarifying live output guarantees and burst throughput in contract
messages:
From: James Holtz <james.holtz@auroradata.com>
To: elliot_price@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: 2027-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Live delivery guarantees for streaming vs batched endpoints

Elliot —

Thanks for the draft SLA you sent last week. Our legal and infra teams reviewed it and have two broad areas where we need clearer commitments before we can complete procurement: 1) how you define and measure the live output guarantee for streaming endpoints (time-to-first-token and token emission rate expectations), and 2) how you handle short-duration bursts versus sustained throughput on non-streaming (batch) endpoints.

High-level asks from Aurora:
- A clear metric and measurement window for "time-to-first-token" on streaming endpoints, including P50/P95 targets and how warm vs cold start is accounted for.
- Expected sustained tokens/sec per endpoint and documented behavior for bursts (e.g., 30s spikes at 5x sustained rate) — will there be throttling, queuing, or graceful degradation?
- Contract language for exceptions during scheduled maintenance, regional failover, or model rollouts.
- A short acceptance test plan we can run against a staging endpoint (30–90 minute window) to validate.

I've attached our vendor_questions.xlsx (see referenced items in the PDF you sent). Can we set up a 30-minute sync to walk through? Prefer this week so procurement can keep to our timeline.

Thanks,
James Holtz
Head of Platform Operations
Aurora Data

Attachments: vendor_questions.xlsx

From: elliot_price@redwood.com
To: James Holtz <james.holtz@auroradata.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live delivery guarantees for streaming vs batched endpoints

James —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front; happy to walk through details on a call. Proposed summary we can use to update the SLA draft:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints
- Definition: TTFT is measured from ingress of a complete request to the first token successfully emitted by the model stream. Measurement window: single-request measurement; aggregate SLOs are reported on a per-endpoint basis.
- Baseline commitment: P95 TTFT <= 450ms under provisioned capacity for requests with prompt <= 1k tokens and typical model contexts. P50 typically ~120–220ms depending on model size.
- Cold starts: Cold-start measurements are excluded from the baseline SLO for the first 10 minutes after an idle period; warmup behavior and pre-warming options available as part of Dedicated contracts.

2) Token emission/sustained throughput expectations
- Streaming endpoints: we commit to a sustained emission baseline (e.g., 200 tokens/sec per provisioned vGPU equivalent) and document per-model profiles in the model catalog. Bursts: short bursts (<= 30s) of up to 4x sustained rate will be accepted where capacity allows; if capacity constraints apply we will apply graceful pacing with a documented fallback (queue and best-effort ramp).
- Batch/non-streaming endpoints: latency SLAs are measured as request completion time. Sustained throughput is provisioned by reserved capacity; spikes beyond provisioned capacity may introduce queuing or rate limiting — we'll define burst credit policies in the SLA appendix.

3) Exceptions and operational windows
- Scheduled maintenance: notified 72 hours ahead; scheduled windows do not count toward uptime calculations.
- Rollouts and model swaps: canary windows are excluded for the first 30 minutes of a canary unless otherwise agreed.

4) Acceptance test plan
- We'll provide a 60-minute staging runbook with scripted calls (attached CSV of test vectors) and a lightweight monitoring agent that captures TTFT and token emission traces.

I'll loop Ben for exact legal phrasing and Marissa for the performance test artifacts. If that summary looks reasonable I'll update the SLA PDF and send a tracked-changes version. Meeting: I'm available 11–11:30 or 15–15:30 PT this week.

—Elliot
Elliot Price
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: throughput-test-plan.csv

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: James Holtz <james.holtz@auroradata.com>, elliot_price@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live delivery guarantees for streaming vs batched endpoints

James —

Adding a few operational notes that we'll include in the SLA appendix. I quoted Elliot's summary below and added specifics for carveouts and SLAs: 

> TTFT: P95 <= 450ms under provisioned capacity; cold starts excluded for first 10m.

Operational additions:
- Burst credit bucket: each Dedicated reservation includes a burst credit pool (measured in token-seconds). Customers may consume credits for short spikes; if the bucket is depleted we will enforce soft-pacing rather than hard drop. The bucket model will be parameterized per commitment size.
- Emergency fallbacks: in multi-region setups we provide automatic reroute to a warm-region endpoint for up to 15 minutes while we remediate. Failover latency is out-of-band from TTFT SLOs and covered under an availability carveout.
- Observability: we will provide token-level traces and per-request TTFT metrics (P50/P95/P99) for the rolling 30-day window in the Console.

I'll propose concrete contract text in tracked changes. Marissa, can you attach the test run CSV and the latency trace extract from last week's perf run? Karthik — please review the burst credit draft and advise on numbers for AUR-2027-045.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: James Holtz <james.holtz@auroradata.com>
To: elliot_price@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: 2027-08-04T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live delivery guarantees for streaming vs batched endpoints

Elliot / Ben —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few follow-ups from procurement and platform: 
- The 450ms P95 is acceptable if the measurement window and traffic profile are clearly defined. Please add a definition for "typical model contexts" (which models and prompt sizes) so we can align test vectors.
- For bursts, procurement wants hard guarantees about degradation behavior. "Soft-pacing" is acceptable, but we need a cap on worst-case tail latency under burst exhaustion (for example, 95th percentile completion time during burst conditions).
- Cold starts exclusion: can you provide the telemetry definition that flags an instance as "cold" and confirm whether pre-warm is available in Dedicated?
- Please include a short sample clause for credits/penalties if the provider misses the P95 TTFT in a given month (we can start with a credit ladder tied to severity).

We'll run the staging acceptance test on Aug 10 in your staging environment if you send the runbook and target endpoints by EOD Aug 6.

Regards,
James

From: elliot_price@redwood.com
To: James Holtz <james.holtz@auroradata.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-05T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live delivery guarantees for streaming vs batched endpoints

James —

Thanks — attaching an updated SLA draft (Redwood_SLA-draft-v3.pdf) with:
- An explicit list of model context classes we will test against (small, medium, large model profiles) and the prompt-size buckets used for TTFT measurement.
- Telemetry definition for "cold": an instance is considered cold if it has received zero requests in the previous 10 minutes and requires container spin-up. Docs include the exact metric flags we emit.
- Burst behavior appendix with the burst credit bucket math and a sample worst-case tail-latency table when the credit bucket is exhausted (we commit to soft-pacing and provide a 95th percentile bound for completion under exhausted-burst conditions).
- A preliminary credit ladder for missed monthly P95 TTFT (tiered credits: 5% for first breach, 10% beyond repeated breaches) — legal to confirm.

I've also attached the throughput-test-results.csv (sample traces from the staging run). Please review and let us know any tweaks to the acceptance test vectors. If this looks good we'll send a redline for signatures next week.

Call: I'll stand by for a short sync Aug 6 at 11:00 PT to walk through the appendix if that works for your team.

—Elliot
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA-draft-v3.pdf; throughput-test-results.csv
